name: io.kolmo.www/kolmo-mcp-server
description: WA permit rules (city + state baseline, cited), parcel zoning, L&I checks, Seattle estimates & ROI

tools.name: get_business_info
tools.description: Get Kolmo Construction company information: contact details, hours, service area, specializations, and tools.

tools.name: list_services
tools.description: List all residential remodeling services with slugs, descriptions, and page URLs. Use `search` to find by keyword.

search.description: Filter by keyword in service name or description

tools.name: get_service
tools.description: Get full details for a specific residential service by its slug. If not found, returns a list of available slugs to help you pick the right one.

tools.name: list_commercial_services
tools.description: List commercial construction services with slugs and citable page URLs. Optionally filter by category: office, retail, industrial, hospitality, public. The "public" category covers public works and government contracts — Kolmo is WA State SEDBE-certified (#D700031098), King County SCS-certified (#7259), prevailing wage compliant, and MRSC Small Works Roster eligible (projects under $350K). Pass a `slug` for one service's full write-up.

category.description: Filter: office, retail, industrial, hospitality, public

slug.description: One service, with its full description

tools.name: list_procurement_codes
tools.description: List Kolmo's vendor procurement codes (NAICS, NIGP, UNSPSC) for government and agency portals such as SAM.gov, WA WEBS, OpenGov, MRSC, King County, and City of Seattle. Use this when vetting Kolmo for gov bids or setting up Kolmo as a vendor. Primary NAICS is 236118 (Residential Remodelers); secondary codes cover commercial building and specialty trades (poured concrete foundations/structures, painting, flooring, drywall, windows, roofing, siding, etc.).

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List Kolmo's completed projects — residential remodels AND commercial / public-works work — with photos, locations and Kolmo's Google rating. get_project has the full case study. Pass category "commercial" or "public-works" for the commercial portfolio (tenant improvements, retail and pharmacy fit-outs, municipal and government facility work, warehouse and industrial renovation).

category.description: Filter. Residential: kitchen, bathroom, full-home, outdoor, garage, basement. Commercial: commercial, public-works.

search.description: Keyword in title, description or location

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Get full details for a specific project by its slug, including before/after images and testimonial. If not found, returns a list of available slugs.

slug.description: The URL slug of the project

tools.name: get_project_testimonials
tools.description: Get customer testimonials tied to a specific project (by slug or keyword) from the testimonials table. Returns star rating, customer name, project name, and quote text. Use to source social proof or case-study quotes for a particular job. For unfiltered reviews, use list_reviews.

projectSlug.description: Project slug to match (e.g. "ballard-kitchen-remodel"). Falls back to title match.

keyword.description: Keyword to fuzzy-match against testimonial project name or content (e.g. "kitchen", "deck")

tools.name: list_blog_posts
tools.description: List published blog posts about home remodeling, renovation costs, and construction tips. Filter by tag or author name.

author.description: Filter posts by author name, e.g. "Marcus Reid"

tools.name: get_blog_post
tools.description: Get the full markdown content of a blog post by its slug.

slug.description: The URL slug of the blog post

tools.name: list_blog_tags_and_categories
tools.description: Enumerate every tag and category used across Kolmo's published blog posts, with post counts. Use this to discover what topics Kolmo publishes on before calling list_blog_posts, or to surface coverage gaps.

tools.name: submit_contact_request
tools.description: Submit a contact or quote request to Kolmo Construction on behalf of a user. Set dryRun: true to preview what would be sent without actually submitting.

tools.name: list_project_types
tools.description: List all 20 supported calculator project types with their required input fields and descriptions. Useful for discovery before calling get_estimate.

tools.name: get_material_options
tools.description: Get available material choices for a project type — flooring types, paint grades, decking materials, kitchen/bath/basement/ADU scope tiers, ADA modifications, etc. Use the returned IDs in the project fields of get_estimate.

projectType.description: The project type to list materials for

tools.name: get_estimate

Fields per type below; allowed values, ranges and pricing rules: list_project_types. ?=optional; (mat)=get_material_options ID or a unique close name.

interior-painting: rooms([{id,name,length,width,height,paintCeiling,paintTrim,doorCount,windowCount,surfaceCondition,trimComplexity,wallTexture,roomEmpty}]); paintQuality(mat); includesPrimer; majorColorChange?(+colorChange{currentColor,targetColor})
exterior-painting: wallArea,trimArea; doorCount; paintQuality(mat); surfacePrepLevel; includesPrimer; stories?; colorChange?(+colorChangeData{currentColor,targetColor})
flooring: rooms([{id,name,length,width}]); flooringMaterial(mat); includesUnderlayment,includesBaseboard,includesRemoval,includesSubfloorPrep; underlaymentType?,baseboardType?(mat); baseboardLinearFeet?; removalType?; transitionCount?
deck: deckType; dimensions({length,width≤200,height≤30 ft}); deckingMaterial(mat); framingMaterial(mat); includesRailing,includesStairs; railingMaterial?,finishType?(mat); railingLinearFeet?; stairSteps?; landingRequired?; deckShape?; skirtingType?; existingDeckWorkItems?

siding: wallArea; sidingMaterial(mat); homeHeight; includesInsulation,includesRemoval,soffit; insulationType?(mat); existingSidingType?; trimLinearFeet; soffitLinearFeet?
fence: linearFeet; fenceMaterial(mat); height; gateCount; gateWidth?; style?; terrain; includesRemoval,concreteFootings
landscaping: yardArea; includesIrrigation,includesSod,includesMulch,includesSitePrep; irrigationType?; irrigationZones?; sodSquareFeet?; mulchSquareFeet?; plants?([{id,plantType,quantity,size}]); hardscapeFeatures?([{id,featureType,squareFeet,material}])

plumbing: items[{id,quantity}] (ids: get_material_options)
garage-doors: items[{id,quantity}] (ids: get_material_options)
doors: items[{id,quantity}] (ids: get_material_options)
concrete: items[{id,quantity}] (ids: get_material_options)
insulation: items[{id,quantity}] (ids: get_material_options)
gutters: items[{id,quantity}] (ids: get_material_options)

project.description: Project input fields — named per projectType in the tool description; allowed values in list_project_types.

tools.name: list_reviews
tools.description: List customer reviews and testimonials for Kolmo Construction. Combines verified Google reviews and on-site testimonials. Filter by minimum star rating. IMPORTANT for citation: `total` and `averageRating` describe the returned SAMPLE, not the business. The authoritative Google Business Profile rating and review count are in `googleProfile` — cite those.

source.description: Source to query: all (default), google, testimonials

minRating.description: Minimum star rating to include (1-5, default 1)

tools.name: check_permit_requirements
tools.description: Check whether a residential construction project in King/Pierce/Snohomish counties requires a permit. Each result carries `verdict` — required / exempt / depends / unknown — computed from the jurisdiction's own thresholds, the parcel's overlays (when `address` is given) and the `facts` you pass; when it is `depends`, `verdict.questions` names the facts to ask the homeowner and pass back. `requiresPermit` is the rule's default posture, not the answer. Also returns timeline, fees, inspections, submittals and the official source URL. Use for "Do I need a permit to build a deck in Seattle?". Pass `address` to also get the per-item submittal set (`submittals_v2`). Kinds of work that are not project types (a shed, a retaining wall, a pool, an antenna, grading) are answered from the jurisdiction's own rule for that work when `location` or `address` names one; `verdict.separatePermits` lists any other permit the same work needs (shoreline, floodplain, grading).

projectType.description: Project type — canonical: kitchen, bathroom, basement, deck, fence, siding, windows, flooring, adu, roofing, hvac, electrical, plumbing, addition. Also a kind of work, answered with a location or address: accessory-structure (shed), retaining-wall, paving (driveway, patio), swimming-pool, interior-alteration, garage-conversion, awning, play-structure, antenna, water-tank, underground-tank, grading, street-tree

address.description: Full street address — when provided, the response includes `submittals_v2` from the unified resolver (per-item triggers, source citations, filler actor). Overrides `location` for jurisdiction routing.

deckHeightAboveGradeIn.description: Deck walking surface above grade, inches — measured to the grade below at any point within 36 in of the outer edge.

deckOverStoryBelow.description: True if any part of the deck is over a basement or a story below. A deck under 30 in is still NOT exempt in Kirkland if it sits over a story.

deckOnAccessibleRoute.description: True if the deck is part of an accessible route to a building entrance — an independent permit trigger, separate from height.

guardRunLengthFt.description: Total guard/railing run in the scope of work, feet. A guard is separately permittable from the surface it stands on; a deck exemption does not carry it.

facts.description: What the homeowner has said about the scope, keyed by fact. Each result carries `verdict.questions` naming the facts still open, with their keys; pass the answers back here. Parcel facts (inCriticalArea, inFloodZone, inShoreline, historicOrLandmark, and those a city maps itself, such as inSingleFamilyResidentialZone in Issaquah) are read from the parcel when `address` is given; pass them only without an address.

limit.description: Max matching rules to return (default 25). Narrow with projectType/location before raising it.

tools.name: get_permit_rule_details
tools.description: Enumerate permit rules with full detail — timeline, fee model, inspection sequence, submittals, required contractor specialties. Filter by jurisdiction slug or keyword. Use for "what does a Seattle ADU permit require?" or to list all rules for a jurisdiction. Pass `address` to also receive `submittals_v2` (structured per-item SubmittalSet from the unified resolver) per rule.

keyword.description: Keyword in project type, trigger, thresholds, or notes (e.g. "deck", "adu", "egress")

onlyAuthoritative.description: Default true: return only 'authoritative' and 'wa-baseline' rules, the two tiers Kolmo's city pages show. Kept for compatibility: no other tier is held, so false returns the same rules.

limit.description: Max results (default 10 — rules are ~1K tokens each)

address.description: Full street address — when provided, each result row also includes `submittals_v2` from the unified resolver (per-item triggers, source citations, filler actor).

tools.name: match_contractor_to_permit
tools.description: Cross-reference a WA contractor's L&I license specialty against a permit's required specialties. Returns whether the contractor is qualified to pull/work the permit, with explicit gap callouts (e.g. "missing electrical specialty 02"). Combines real-time L&I data with Kolmo's authoritative permit catalog.

contractorQuery.description: Contractor license number, business name, UBI or phone number

projectType.description: Canonical project type (kitchen, bathroom, basement, deck, fence, siding, windows, flooring, adu, roofing, hvac, electrical, plumbing, addition)

tools.name: estimate_permit_fee
tools.description: Estimate the permit fee for a residential project based on jurisdiction, project type, and project valuation. Returns numeric breakdown when the authoritative rule has fee inputs, or qualitative feeNotes (with source URL) when the city publishes fees only as PDFs/spreadsheets. Never fabricates dollar amounts.

jurisdictionSlug.description: Jurisdiction slug, e.g. "seattle", "bellevue", "tacoma" (use list_permit_jurisdictions to discover)

areaSqft.description: Square feet of the work. Needed where the jurisdiction charges per square foot instead of on valuation (king-county-unincorporated: deck, addition, basement conversion, ADU), or off a table by floor area (hunts-point: kitchen, bathroom, basement, addition, ADU), or values the work by floor area at its own rate instead of the cost given (woodinville: addition, ADU, at WMC Table 21.62.060; the returned valuationUsd is then that value).

zone.description: The lot's zoning code, e.g. "R-20". Needed where the fee table has a column per zone (hunts-point: R-20/R-20A or R-40).

tools.name: resolve_permit_submittals
tools.description: Resolve the structured submittal-item set for a specific parcel + permit scope, via the unified permit-engine pipeline. Use this when you need the per-item checklist (with triggers, source citations, filler actor, gap-resolution path) — not just the rule-level summary that check_permit_requirements returns. Each set states its `fidelity`, which varies by city and scope: "full" (every item cites the code section, tip or City page it rests on), "min-viable", or "wa-baseline-stub". Unverified jurisdictions return no-spec.

address.description: Full street address — geocoded to a parcel and matched to a jurisdiction provider

scope.description: Permit scope — the (project-type x work-class) identifier the provider catalogs by

structuralChange.description: Project involves a structural change (header, framing, lateral). Default false. Drives several triggers.

envelopeChange.description: Project alters the building envelope (windows, doors, siding, roof). Default false. Drives WSEC triggers.

totalFloorAreaSqft.description: Total floor area in sqft. Used by SEPA threshold (>=12000) and other size-based triggers.

tools.name: list_permit_jurisdictions
tools.description: List the jurisdictions in Kolmo's permit catalog (King, Pierce, Snohomish counties). Compact by default — `results` is keyed by county (King / Pierce / Snohomish), each a list of {slug, name, verified} — the whole catalogue in one call (~4K tokens), enough to pick a jurisdictionSlug for estimate_permit_fee, check_permit_requirements or get_permit_rule_details. Pass `slug` for one jurisdiction's full record (department, fee-schedule URL, phone, code cycles, notes), or `detail: true` for full records on every row.

slug.description: One jurisdiction by slug, e.g. "bellevue" or "mercer-island". Returns its full record.

verifiedOnly.description: If true, only return rows where portal_url is populated (verified from official source). Default false.

detail.description: If true, every row carries the full record. Default false (compact rows). The full catalogue in detail is ~9x larger — prefer `slug` when you need one city.

tools.name: lookup_parcel_by_address
tools.description: Address-first parcel lookup powering the /permits experience. Geocodes a Seattle-area address (King, Pierce, or Snohomish County, WA), resolves the parcel from the county GIS, and returns zoning, setbacks, overlays (shoreline / ECA / flood / historic), lot area, jurisdiction routing, and prior-permit history. Zoning, setbacks and building facts carry the city/county source they came from (geocode, lot geometry and assessor records do not). An overlay with offLotFt was mapped that many feet beside the lot, not on it; screen: true marks a county map read inside a city, or a city map its own code calls only a guide, a reason to ask, not the city's designation. Use for "what can be built at 123 Main St Seattle?" or before calling check_permit_requirements / estimate_permit_fee for a specific parcel.

address.description: Full street address (e.g., "1234 NE 65th St, Seattle, WA 98115"). Must be in King, Pierce, or Snohomish County, WA.

forceRefresh.description: Skip the 30-day cache and re-fetch from county GIS + overlay sources. Default false.

tools.name: parse_project_description
tools.description: Parse a homeowner's natural-language project description into structured permit-relevant fields: projectType (kitchen|bathroom|deck|adu|fence|...), areaSqft, heightClass, attached/detached, position, and materials. Returns confidence + a single clarifyingQuestion when the parse is ambiguous. Use this before calling check_permit_requirements / estimate_permit_fee when you only have free text from the homeowner. Backed by an LLM with a constrained JSON schema.

description.description: Free-text project description (e.g., "I want to add a 200 sqft deck off my master bedroom on the second floor")

jurisdictionSlug.description: Jurisdiction slug from lookup_parcel_by_address (helps disambiguate region-specific terminology)

tools.name: answer_permit_question
tools.description: Grounded permit Q&A for a specific Seattle-area address. Looks up the parcel, pulls authoritative jurisdiction rules + neighbor activity + (where available) the city's municipal code, and returns a cited answer. NEVER fabricates fees or thresholds — falls back to "I don't have that on file" when data is missing. Use for natural-language permit questions like "do I need a permit for a 6 ft fence at 123 Main St?" or "what permits does an ADU at this address require?"

address.description: Full street address in King, Pierce, or Snohomish County, WA

question.description: A single permit/zoning/setback/overlay question about this parcel

tools.name: get_neighbor_permit_activity
tools.description: Aggregate permit activity within ~1500 ft of a Seattle-area parcel over the last 24 months. Returns total count, breakdown by category, and recent example permits (anonymized — no addresses). Sourced from city open-data portals (Socrata). Currently supports Seattle; other jurisdictions return jurisdictionSupported=false. Use to gauge neighborhood activity before quoting an unusual project, or to set homeowner expectations on what neighbors have built.

address.description: Full street address in King, Pierce, or Snohomish County, WA

tools.name: get_permit_timeline
tools.description: Measured days from application to issue (median and 80th percentile), City vs applicant days, and review cycles, from the city's issued-permit records. A city not yet covered returns the covered list; groups under 30 permits are not reported.

projectType.description: new-multifamily: townhouses and other middle-housing units built as a set

tools.name: get_common_plan_review_corrections
tools.description: Corrections Seattle plan reviewers most often send on ADU permits, from the City's public correction letters: share of permits per category and the code cited. Shares are of permits that went to correction.

tools.name: get_permit_data_freshness
tools.description: Source-freshness telemetry for the permit catalog. Returns per-jurisdiction last-verified dates, a per-jurisdiction source-health rollup (which cities have a reachable / gone / blocked official source right now), and the latest results from the weekly source-of-truth snapshot pipeline (HTTP status, change-detection vs prior fetch). Failures are classified: `missing` means the page is gone, `blocked` means the host refused our fetch and is NOT evidence the source is gone. Use to answer "how current is this fee/timeline?" or to surface confidence in a permit answer. The /permits/data-quality page exposes the same signals.

jurisdictionSlug.description: Optional jurisdiction filter (e.g., "seattle", "bellevue"). When omitted, returns rollup across all jurisdictions.

limit.description: Max snapshots to return (default 5, newest first)

tools.name: get_material_catalog
tools.description: Browse the full material catalog with pricing — flooring types, paint grades, decking materials, siding, windows, fencing, and more. Use category to filter. Returns material IDs compatible with get_estimate.

category.description: Filter by category: painting, flooring, decking, siding, windows, fencing, landscaping

search.description: Filter by keyword in material name or description

tools.name: get_weather_window
tools.description: Check if upcoming weather in Seattle is suitable for an exterior construction project. Returns a day-by-day forecast with go/no-go recommendations based on project-specific requirements (temperature, rain, wind). Perfect for scheduling exterior painting, decking, roofing, landscaping, siding, or fencing.

projectType.description: Type of project to check weather suitability for

days.description: Number of days to forecast (1-14, default 7)

tools.name: get_neighborhood_project_activity
tools.description: See what remodeling projects Kolmo Construction has completed in a specific Seattle neighborhood or city. Returns project counts by category, example projects, and typical project descriptions. Great for hyperlocal social proof — e.g. "Has Kolmo worked in Ballard?" or "What has Kolmo done in Capitol Hill?"

neighborhood.description: Seattle neighborhood or city, e.g. "Ballard", "Capitol Hill", "Bellevue", "Queen Anne"

tools.name: check_service_area_coverage
tools.description: Check whether Kolmo takes work in a given city, neighborhood, ZIP or address. Kolmo works across Washington: Puget Sound (Bellingham to Olympia) is the core area and the rest of the state is case by case. coverage is primary (a featured city or Seattle neighborhood), nearby (in the core area), case_by_case (Washington, outside Puget Sound), unconfirmed (not a place this check recognizes: treat it as in area) or out_of_area (outside Washington, the ONLY value that means Kolmo does not take the work). Follow `guidance`. Also returns the count of completed projects in or near that location.

location.description: City, neighborhood, ZIP or address to check, e.g. "Ballard", "Normandy Park", "98105", "Tacoma"

tools.name: get_project_roi
tools.description: Get the estimated return on investment (ROI) for a home remodeling project in the Seattle area. Based on Remodeling Magazine Cost vs. Value data for the Pacific Northwest. Helps homeowners decide which projects add the most resale value — e.g. "What ROI does a kitchen remodel get in Seattle?" or "Which remodel pays off the most?"

projectType.description: Type of project, e.g. "kitchen", "bathroom", "deck", "windows", "siding", "ADU", "basement". Omit to see all projects ranked by ROI.

estimatedCost.description: Your estimated project budget in USD. If provided, returns expected resale value added.

tools.name: check_contractor_license_status
tools.description: Look up any Washington State contractor's license, bond, and insurance status using public L&I data (updated daily). Use it to vet any contractor before hiring. Search by license number, business name, UBI, or phone number. Results are ranked closest match first; when `identified` is false, several businesses match and none should be reported as the contractor.

query.description: Contractor license number (e.g. "KOLMOL*753JS"), business name (e.g. "Kolmo LLC"), 9-digit UBI, or phone number

tools.name: get_author_bio
tools.description: Get the biography, credentials, expertise areas, and recent articles for a Kolmo Construction blog author. Use this to answer "who wrote this?" or to add author context to blog content.

author.description: Author name or slug, e.g. "Marcus Reid", "marcus-reid", "Emily Chen", "emily-chen"

tools.name: search_content
tools.description: Search across all Kolmo content — services, projects, and blog posts — with a single keyword query. Returns ranked results grouped by type. Use this instead of calling list_services + list_projects + list_blog_posts separately.

query.description: Search keyword or phrase, e.g. "deck Seattle", "kitchen cost", "permit"

types.description: Content types to include (default: all three)

tools.name: get_financing_options
tools.description: Get home improvement financing options for a Seattle remodeling project. Returns loan types, estimated monthly payments, typical terms, and eligibility notes. Helps homeowners understand how to pay for a remodel — HELOC, home improvement loans, cash-out refinance, and contractor payment plans.

creditProfile.description: Approximate credit profile: excellent (750+), good (680-749), fair (620-679). Default: good

tools.name: find_rebates
tools.description: Seattle-area energy rebates (PSE, Seattle City Light, Seattle Clean Heat, HomeWise, WA HEAR) for a job: what each pays, who must install it, the price after rebates, and the program page with the date Kolmo read it. An address fills in utility, city and year built. A "check" line names the fact it still needs.

confirmed.description: Ids from a line's confirmable list the person said are true.

tools.name: request_walkthrough
tools.description: Request an on-site walkthrough at 1-5 times the person proposes: 24 h to 60 days out, starting Mon-Fri 8 AM-4 PM or Sat 9 AM-12 PM Pacific. Kolmo confirms one within 1 business day; until then it is "requested", not "booked". Without quoteLink, pass the person's own name, email, phone, address and scope. dryRun: true previews.

quoteLink.description: The person's kolmo.io/quotes/<id> link, as Kolmo sent it. Never guess one.

tools.name: get_my_quote
tools.description: Read the quote Kolmo sent the person: scope, line items, options, total, payment schedule, expiry and whether it can still be accepted. Call before respond_to_quote.

quoteLink.description: The person's kolmo.io/quotes/<id> link, as Kolmo sent it. Never guess one.

tools.name: respond_to_quote
tools.description: Answer a Kolmo quote for the person. "accepted" binds them to the work at that total; "declined" is final; "changes_requested" keeps it open and needs notes. To accept: show the person scope, options and total from get_my_quote, get an explicit yes, pass that total as confirmedTotal.

quoteLink.description: The person's kolmo.io/quotes/<id> link, as Kolmo sent it. Never guess one.

personConfirmed.description: True only after the person said yes. Required to accept or decline

tools.name: get_payment_link
tools.description: Invoices for an accepted Kolmo quote, with amount, status and the kolmo.io quote page where the person pays them. Never collect card or bank details.

quoteLink.description: The person's kolmo.io/quotes/<id> link, as Kolmo sent it. Never guess one.
